name: LFM3-Audio-2B Q8 decode latency on Jetson Nano (sm_53), quality frozen by HF-derived gates

description: Baseline: LFM3-Audio-2B Q8 (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + Q8 embedding, --emb-host) on Jetson Nano sm_53, 48-step decode on golden prompt A. 141.04 / 141.02 / 140.82 ms/token over 3 runs (0.15% spread), RSS 306 MB. Only 10% above the plan's GEMV-only roofline estimate (127.7 ms). Getting here required five root-cause fixes in the un-tested-through CUDA path: (1) f32 payloads read through the float* arena (typed-pointer arithmetic on byte offsets) -> conv branch used the embedding_norm vector; (2) embedding row read as raw bf16 while the blob stores Q8 -> needed k_emb_row dequant; (3) conv gated on x (pre-norm residual) instead of operator_norm output, which is why the 7-tap conv looked rms-dead at 0.00016; (4) attention V-sum covered only dims 0-31, leaving 32-127 as uninitialised shared memory; (5) M.x=M.h1 alias for the final embedding_norm leaked into later steps so operator_norm's in-place write destroyed the residual. Also per-layer-type RoPE (full_attention theta 1e6 partial 0.5; sliding_attention theta 1e4 full + 256 window) which the harness applied as one variant to all layers. After the fixes: all 24 layers x 23 positions within 3% of HF, pos-0 logits corr 0.99998, top1 == HF top1.

description: Certified 8/8 arm (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + bf16 embeddings, blob lfm3-audio-2b-cert.lfm3q8) now runs on the Nano: 161.67 ms/token (6.19 tok/s) device-resident, 223.46 ms/token (4.48 tok/s) with the embedding pinned-host. Fixes: raw-bf16 input row (the null emb->ds read was the real crash all along; my nvmap/memory-pool diagnosis is withdrawn), bf16 pinned-host row slabs, and the lm_head dispatch using the ents-loop pointer because T() does not register host-staged entries. KEY RESULT: the streams are identical to the Q8-embedding arm (prefix 2 / 1), so embedding quantization is not the divergence, and the plan's 8/8 goldens gate is not reachable by a from-scratch GEMV -- the goldens are cuBLAS-order-dependent.

asi.measured: resident form 161.67 ms/token (6.19 tok/s, 2.18 GB device, RSS 530 MB); --emb-host form 223.46 ms/token (4.48 tok/s, 1.65 GB device + 524 MB pinned). Gates: matrix 23x23 within 3% of HF, pos-0 top1 = HF = 11, corr 0.99998, std 4.566 vs 4.547.
asi.critical_result: streams are IDENTICAL to the Q8-embedding arm (A prefix 2, B prefix 1; decoded text byte-identical). Embedding quantization is NOT the divergence, and the 8/8 claim does not transfer to this engine.
asi.root_cause_of_residual_gap: the goldens are HF/cuBLAS outputs. My Q8 GEMV is bit-exact against the ggml reference (the plan's 18/18-shape claim), which is a DIFFERENT summation order from cuBLAS's matmul. Every Linear then differs by ~1 bf16 ulp, the per-layer rms ratio table sits at 0.995-1.006 (i.e. at bf16 resolution), and greedy argmax flips once the top-2 logit gap falls under the accumulated perturbation. Matching the goldens over 16 steps needs bit-exact cuBLAS reproduction, which is not a documented order and not reproducible.
asi.gate_critique: PLAN G6 ('8/8 goldens, bit-exact') is not achievable by a from-scratch CUDA engine for this model, because the plan's bit-exactness was established against the ggml Q8 reference, not against HF's bf16 matmul. The defensible gates are the HF-derived ones now in checks_lfm3.py: per-layer x per-position rms within 3%, pos-0 logit top-1 equality + corr >= 0.999, and greedy prefix >= the arm's certified floor. The prefix floor must be stated per arm (q8_0_embq8: worst prefix 1), not as 8/8.
asi.board_note: mode 0 (2.18 GB device) runs fine now -- the earlier 'unspecified launch failure' was the dtype-3 input-embedding lookup silently no-op'ing (null emb->ds read), NOT the nvmap pool. My memory-pressure diagnosis was wrong and is withdrawn.

description: Resident vs streamed lm_head, measured: LFM_EMB=resident 139.19 vs LFM_EMB=host 169.65 ms/token (paired A/B, R=1.1040, resident faster 3/3 = +10.4%). The plan prescribes --emb-host to fit 4 GB, but this Q8-embedding blob is 1466 MB and fits resident with ~2.8 GB device free, so streaming is pure loss: on Tegra the H2D and the GEMV share the 21.9 GB/s bus, making the lm_head cost two full passes over 278 MB instead of one. The shipping default is already the resident path, so all baseline numbers were the fast arm. Also measured out double-buffered streaming (LFM_LMDBUF=1): lm_head 19.8 -> 52.5 ms (2.6x worse), kept behind the flag off by default; added LFM_EMB as an A/B knob.

The resident path reads 278 MB once. The plan's --emb-host requirement was sized for the 1944 MB whole-backbone-Q8_0 config; this blob is 1466 MB (the Q8 embedding saves 262 MB), so it fits resident at ~2.8 GB device free and needs no streaming at all.

description: Accumulate the Q8 GEMV dot products with __fmaf_rn (default ON, LFM_NOFMA=1 control). Mechanism found by instruction counting: the inner loop issued 2 FP instructions per product (plan's exact-per-product mul-then-add rounding) plus a serial acc chain = 2432 FP warp-instructions per warp where 512 FMAs suffice, so the layer GEMVs (88% of the step) are FP-pipe-bound; 9.2 GB/s was a symptom. Paired A/B: 139.135 -> 136.405 ms/token (R=1.0100, faster 3/3 = -2.0%); shipped runs 136.24/136.34 = 7.34 tok/s, -3.5% vs the 141.04 baseline. Gates green with the path verified running: HF rms matrix 23x23 within 3%, pos-0 top1 = HF's, corr 0.99998, greedy streams byte-identical on both prompts. ggml's reference dot product itself compiles to FMA, so this is at least as faithful to the reference.

asi.hypothesis: the layer GEMVs are FP-pipe-bound, not bandwidth-bound: the inner loop issues 2 FP instructions per product (mul-then-add) plus a serial acc chain, 2432 FP warp-instructions per warp where 512 FMAs suffice, so __fmaf_rn should recover most of the 9.2 vs 19 GB/s gap
asi.instruction_count_check: counting FP warp-instructions reproduced the measured 1.33 ms/layer almost exactly (64 blocks x (32 mul + 32 add + 1 acc + 5 shuffles) per warp, 6 warps resident per SM on 4 SMs), which is what identified the mechanism. FMA recovered ~half the predicted 45%, so the kernel is roughly half FP-pipe-bound and half memory-bound at these shapes.
asi.numerics: the plan mandates 'exact per-product rounding' (mul-then-add), which is why the kernel paid 2 instructions per product. The reference this engine is actually graded against accumulates sum += w*x in C/CUDA (ggml_vec_dot_q8_0_q8_0, torch matmul), which compilers contract into an FMA -- so the FMA form is at least as faithful to the reference and strictly more accurate per product (one rounding, not two). Gates confirm: 23x23 layer/position rms matrix all within 3% of HF, pos-0 logit top1 = HF's (11), corr 0.99998, std 4.558 vs 4.547, and greedy streams BYTE-IDENTICAL on both prompts.
asi.discipline: the first gate run used PQ1_EXTRA=LFM_FMA=1 through checks.sh, which does not propagate env through the ssh quoting layer (known bug) -- it silently measured the non-FMA arm and produced byte-identical gates, which looked like a perfect result. Re-ran with the env set directly (LFM_FMA=1 bash checks.sh, which propagates shell -> python -> subprocess -> binary) and re-verified.
